decisions.location: Deviations from the original study, lines 127-132
decisions.reason: The dependent record type is 'replication' rather than 'reproduction' because the author did not have access to the original study's dataset from Du et al. (2020) and instead downloaded fresh Google Trends search samples (both for alternative keywords 'hoarding' and 'shortage' and for the original keywords 'panic buying' and 'stockpile'). As noted in the prior adjudication and parent supplemental decision, this type correction makes the replication outcome 'successful' (the Panic Buying Index positively predicted COVID-19 infections across both analyses) and renders the reproduction axis outcome_computation inapplicable (undeterminable).

decisions.reason: Under the codebook, outcome_robustness concerns re-analyses of the original study's own dataset, whereas fresh samples constitute a replication. Because the original authors' Google Trends dataset was unavailable and this study analyzed newly downloaded Google Trends samples (confirming a 'successful' replication outcome for Du et al., 2020), the dependent record type is 'replication' and the reproduction axis outcome_robustness is inapplicable (undeterminable).
